purpose: Replace the nonabelian S3 gauge of v5.3 by a pure additive GF(3) translation gauge. Normalize one port of every complementary cycle to colour zero; the remaining constant local state is exactly a normalized proper cycle colouring, equivalently a nowhere-zero cycle-tension pattern. For fixed local states, every Hamiltonian edge becomes one standard Z3 group-colouring disequality.

normalized_cycle_types.definition: For a length-k complementary cycle X with ordered ports 0,...,k-1, let Sigma_k be all proper colourings sigma:V(C_k)->GF(3) with sigma(0)=0.
normalized_cycle_types.count: |Sigma_k|=P_Ck(3)/3=(2^k+2*(-1)^k)/3, because translation by GF(3) acts freely on all proper colourings.
normalized_cycle_types.unique_decomposition: Every proper component colouring c_X has a unique representation c_X(p)=u_X+sigma_X(p), where u_X=c_X(0) in GF(3) and sigma_X in Sigma_k.
normalized_cycle_types.tension_equivalence: The differences sigma_X(p+1)-sigma_X(p) are all nonzero and sum to zero around the cycle. Conversely every nowhere-zero GF(3) tension on C_k integrates uniquely to one sigma in Sigma_k after fixing sigma(0)=0.

c4_control.tension_patterns: These are exactly the six oriented C4 sign patterns with two +1 edges and two -1 edges.
c4_control.relation_to_v5_3: The involution sigma -> -sigma pairs the six normalized types into the three S3-orbit types of v5.3. Thus the former S3 reflection bit is absorbed into the local type and only the additive translation gauge remains global.

quotient_gain_graph.Q: Contract every complementary F-cycle to one node, retain each Hamiltonian edge with its endpoint port labels, and orient the quotient edges arbitrarily.
quotient_gain_graph.state: At quotient node X choose sigma_X in Sigma_k and u_X in GF(3).
quotient_gain_graph.edge_gain: For an oriented Hamiltonian edge e from port p of X to port q of Y define f_sigma(e)=sigma_X(p)-sigma_Y(q).
quotient_gain_graph.constraint: Properness of e is exactly u_Y-u_X != f_sigma(e).
quotient_gain_graph.fixed_type_problem: After fixing all sigma_X, deciding the translations u is exactly an (A,f)-group-colouring instance with A=Z3.
quotient_gain_graph.same_component_edge: For X=Y the translation cancels and the constraint is sigma_X(q)-sigma_X(p)!=0, a pure local-type filter.
quotient_gain_graph.reconstruction: A satisfying pair (sigma,u) reconstructs the original vertex colours by c_X(p)=u_X+sigma_X(p) in linear time.

switching_normal_form.rule: For arbitrary s_X in GF(3), set u'_X=u_X+s_X and f'(X->Y)=f(X->Y)+s_Y-s_X. Then u satisfies f iff u' satisfies f'.
switching_normal_form.tree_zeroing: On a connected quotient, choose a spanning tree and switching values recursively so that every tree-edge gain becomes zero.
switching_normal_form.cycle_rank: If there are m complementary length-k components, Q has m nodes and km Hamiltonian edges, so beta(Q)=km-m+1=(k-1)m+1. Switching therefore leaves linearly many independent cycle-gain coordinates in the worst case; it does not by itself create a small-state algorithm.
switching_normal_form.meaning: Absolute edge gains are gauge-dependent. Only their cycle-space switching class matters for the fixed-type translation subproblem.

literature_alignment.definition: Group colouring uses exactly constraints c(v)-c(u)!=f(e) over an additive Abelian group.
literature_alignment.firewall: When all gains are zero this is ordinary proper 3-colouring, so gain switching or Gaussian elimination alone cannot be treated as a generic polynomial solver for disequality constraints.
literature_alignment.scope: The present source is narrower than arbitrary group-colouring: Q is bounded-degree Eulerian with a distinguished Euler tour, and every gain comes from port values of constant-size normalized cycle types. Generic group-colouring hardness does not by itself close this special carrier.

positive: Removes the S3 nonabelian gauge completely; the only global gauge variable is one ternary translation u_X per complementary component.
Packages every complementary C4 into one of six exact local tension states.
Exposes the residual as a Z3 gain-colouring problem with source-generated gains and immediate witness reconstruction.
Allows canonical switching to zero all tree gains without changing satisfiability.
anti_loop: Do not enumerate |Sigma_k|^m local type assignments.
Do not confuse gain disequalities with a linear equation system; Gaussian elimination solves equalities, while f=0 already contains ordinary 3-COLOR.
Do not enumerate the 3^beta switching classes; beta is linear in the number of components.

next_target.directive: Eliminate or contract the constant local sigma_X choices without enumerating them. Exploit simultaneously that Q is 2k-regular Eulerian with a supplied Euler tour, gains are differences of port values from normalized nowhere-zero C_k tensions, and the hard source has non-selfcrossing constant-size complementary cycles. Seek a polynomial switching/minimax identity, a source-specific group-colouring theorem, or a scoped obstruction.

sources: H.-J. Lai and X. Zhang, Group Colorability of Graphs, Ars Combinatoria 62 (2002), 299-317.
